title: Responder LLMNR/NBT-NS/MDNS Poisoning Runner
goal: Add a controlled Responder runner that poisons LLMNR, NBT-NS, and MDNS within the approved network scope to capture NTLMv2 credential hashes — a core technique in internal network assessments.
scope: Implement a 'responder' runner in workers/runners/responder/ that: (1) Launches Responder (pre-installed on Kali) on the configured network interface within the approved CIDR scope using --interface and listen-only configuration. (2) Runs for a configurable duration (default 10 minutes, max 60 minutes). (3) Captures NTLMv2 hashes from responding hosts, stores them as encrypted artifacts (never plain text). (4) Produces findings: one finding per captured hash with host, username, hash type (NTLMv2), and methodology tags (PTES: Exploitation, WSTG-ATHN, NIST: Credential Access T1557.001). (5) Hash material is stored as a protected secrets_ref — it is never written to stdout, logs, or run API payloads. (6) A new 'intrusive-lan-poisoning' approval gate class is required before this runner dispatches. (7) The runner terminates cleanly on kill-switch. (8) Run profile: 'intrusive-lan-credential-capture'. Responder log output is stored as an artifact for evidence.
generation_reason: LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning via Responder is one of the most effective techniques in internal network assessments and is used in virtually every real LAN pentest. Without it, AegisPT's internal assessment cannot capture credentials that exist on the network. NodeZero includes credential capture as a core internal capability.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Poisoning only within approved CIDR scope. Hash material stored as encrypted artifact only — never in plain text. Requires intrusive approval gate. Time-limited run. No hash cracking in this slice (covered in backlog-73). Kill switch terminates Responder immediately.
